definition_zh: 丑陋的；难看的；丑恶的；险恶的；令人不快的
definition_en: unpleasant to look at, morally bad, or threatening in an unspecified way
core_image: 一张脸皱起来，让人本能地想转开眼睛
scene: 镜子前，孩子画的自画像把鼻子画得歪歪扭扭，他自己也忍不住捂住了嘴。The drawing was so ugly that the whole class burst out laughing.
sceneCN: 这里 ugly 是「难看的、丑陋的」（第 1 个义项：外表不悦目）；句意为那幅画难看得全班都笑出了声。皱起的一张脸让人想转开眼睛，正是这个词的核心画面。

collocations.zh: 丑小鸭；起初不起眼而后出众的人

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「丑陋；丑恶」
形容词加 -ify 构成动词，义为「使变丑」
复合形容词，义为「样子难看的」

senses.title: Unpleasant to look at
senses.definition: unpleasant or unattractive in appearance
senses.definitionCN: 外表上令人不快、不好看的
senses.example: An ugly stain spread across the white tablecloth.
senses.exampleCN: 一块难看的污渍在白桌布上漫开。
senses.why: The word comes from Old Norse uggligr, which carried a sense of something to be dreaded, and the visual sense grew out of that dread.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自古诺斯语 uggligr，本带「令人畏惧」之意，视觉上的「难看」是从畏惧感里长出来的。

senses.title: Morally bad or shameful
senses.definition: morally offensive or shameful in a way that arouses disgust
senses.definitionCN: 道德上令人反感、使人厌恶的
senses.example: The trial exposed the ugly side of the business.
senses.exampleCN: 这场审讯暴露了这门生意丑恶的一面。
senses.why: From something dreadful to look at, the word easily moves to something dreadful to think about.
senses.whyCN: 从「看着可怕」很自然地滑到「想着可怕」，丑陋的外表就转成了丑陋的行为。

senses.title: Threatening or dangerous in an unclear way
senses.definition: used of a situation that looks threatening and may turn violent
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容看起来凶险、可能失控的局面
senses.example: The argument was starting to turn ugly.
senses.exampleCN: 争吵开始变得凶险起来。
senses.why: A scene that makes people wince is also a scene that may explode, so ugly marks rising tension.
senses.whyCN: 让人皱眉的场面往往也是随时会爆开的场面，于是 ugly 又用来标记气氛的紧张。

senses.title: Unpleasantly large or strong
senses.definition: used informally of an amount or problem that is unpleasantly big
senses.definitionCN: 非正式地形容数量或问题大得让人不舒服
senses.example: There is an ugly gap between the two reports.
senses.exampleCN: 两份报告之间有一道大得难看的鸿沟。
senses.why: Anything that makes you pull back your head can be called ugly, including an alarming figure.
senses.whyCN: 任何让你下意识缩头的东西都能叫 ugly，包括一个吓人的数字。

senses.title: Unattractive in a homely way
senses.definition: plain or ugly in appearance but not evil, often said of buildings or objects
senses.definitionCN: 外形朴素难看，但不含恶意，常用来形容建筑或器物
senses.example: They built an ugly block of flats by the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在河边盖了一栋难看的公寓楼。
senses.why: This is the neutral everyday use: nothing dreadful, only an eye that refuses to rest on the thing.
senses.whyCN: 这是最中性的日常用法：并不可怕，只是眼睛不愿在它上面停留。

intro.en: The adjective is Scandinavian in origin and entered English in the Middle Ages.
intro.cn: 这个形容词源于斯堪的纳维亚语，中世纪进入英语。

items.en: Uggligr meant dreadful or to be feared, built on a root meaning fear.
items.cn: uggligr 意为「可怕的、令人畏惧的」，其词根表示恐惧。

items.en: The suffix -ligr corresponds to English -ly, so the word first described a manner rather than a face.
items.cn: 后缀 -ligr 相当于英语 -ly，因此这个词最早形容的是一种样子，而非一张脸。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the northern forms as ugly, still with the sense of fearful.
items.cn: 英语以北方方言形式借入作 ugly，仍保留「可怕」之义。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the sense of frightening had faded and appearance took over.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，「令人恐惧」的意味淡去，外观义占了上风。

items.en: Later centuries extend it to behaviour, situations, and amounts.
items.cn: 此后的几个世纪里，它又扩展到行为、局势与数量。

note.en: The look-alike group collects other -ly words, and the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of appearance.
note.cn: 形近组收集其他以 -ly 收尾的形容词，近义组汇集表示外观的其他形容词。

entries.definition: very much, to a great degree
entries.definitionCN: 极其；非常（只是拼写相近，词源不同）
热切地（只是拼写相近，词源不同）
不好看的；没有吸引力的

normalIntro.en: The word began as a label for what makes people afraid, and the sense slid from dread to looks.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词起初标记让人害怕之物，意义由畏惧滑向外观。

normal.en: Ugly and dread share a northern origin, so a fearful shape becomes a bad-looking one.
normal.cn: ugly 与「畏惧」同出北方语言，可怕的样子就变成了难看的样子。

normal.en: Turn ugly is the phrase where the old fear still shows: the mood becomes dangerous.
normal.cn: turn ugly 这个搭配里还能看见旧日的恐惧：气氛变得危险。

normal.en: Ugly duckling comes from Andersen and means someone plain who grows remarkable.
normal.cn: ugly duckling 出自安徒生，指起初平平而后出众的人。

normal.en: Ugliness is the noun, uglify the verb that means to make ugly.
normal.cn: ugliness 是名词，uglify 是使变丑的动词。

normal.en: Uglier and ugliest double the final consonant before -er and -est.
normal.cn: 比较级 uglier 与最高级 ugliest 都在 -er 与 -est 前把 g 双写。

abstract.en: Picture a face in a funhouse mirror, features pulled sideways.
abstract.cn: 想象哈哈镜里的一张脸，五官被拉向一边。

abstract.en: Hear the crowd turn from laughter to a hard silence.
abstract.cn: 听人群从笑声转为僵硬的沉默。

abstract.en: Then feel the same discomfort when a number on a report is too large.
abstract.cn: 再把同样的不适感挪到一个报表上过大的数字。

examples.en: That building is the ugliest one on the street.
examples.cn: 那栋楼是街上最难看的一栋。

examples.en: The mood in the room turned ugly after the vote.
examples.cn: 投票之后屋里的气氛变得凶险。

examples.en: She refused to believe that an ugly past decides a bright future.
examples.cn: 她不肯相信一段丑恶的过去会决定一个光明的未来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿格丽」——阿格丽小姐一皱眉，整张脸就垮得让人不敢看。

root: 古诺斯语 uggligr（可怕的、可畏的），词根表示「恐惧」，后缀 -ligr 相当于英语 -ly；中古英语北方方言借入作 ugly

sensesIntro.en: One core feeling, unease at what meets the eye, spreads from faces to deeds, moods, and figures.
sensesIntro.cn: 一份核心感受，眼睛见到时的不适，由面孔蔓延到行为、气氛与数字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face that makes you want to look away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张让人想转开眼睛的脸。

branches.en: The visual branch: faces, buildings, and objects that the eye rejects.
branches.cn: 视觉分支：眼睛拒绝停留的脸、建筑与器物。

branches.en: The moral branch, where a deed is as hard to look at as a scar.
branches.cn: 道德分支：一桩行为像伤疤一样让人不敢看。

branches.en: The mood branch, where a scene threatens to break open.
branches.cn: 气氛分支：场面随时可能炸开。

branches.en: The quantity branch, where a figure is unpleasantly large.
branches.cn: 数量分支：一个数字大得让人不适。

branches.en: The plain descriptive sense that most learners meet first.
branches.cn: 最朴素的描写义，也是学习者最先遇到的义项。

intro.en: The word is not built from Latin parts but from a northern suffix attached to a stem of fear.
intro.cn: 这个词不由拉丁部件构成，而是恐惧词干加北方语言后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor here, so the Latin list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 此词没有拉丁语祖先，故拉丁同源词一栏留空。

items.example: Ugly once named what people feared.
items.exampleCN: ugly 曾经指人们畏惧的东西。

items.example: Ugly and lonely both end in -ly as adjectives.
items.exampleCN: ugly 与 lonely 都以 -ly 收尾而作形容词。

items.example: They uglified the square with billboards.
items.exampleCN: 他们用广告牌把广场弄得很难看。

items.example: The ugliness of the plan shocked them.
items.exampleCN: 计划的丑恶让他们震惊。

definition_zh: 最终的；最后的；根本的；极限的；终极的
definition_en: coming at the very end, or being the most basic and extreme form of something
core_image: 一条长路的尽头，最后一面旗插在那里
scene: 登山队在长坡上走了整整一天，抬头时终于看见最后那道山脊上立着界碑。Reaching the summit was the ultimate test of their patience.
sceneCN: 这里 ultimate 是「最终的、终极的」（第 1 个义项：处于最后位置）；句意为登顶是他们对耐心最彻底的考验。长路尽头的那面旗正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「最终；归根到底」
同源名词，义为「最后通牒」
形容词加 -acy 构成名词，义为「终极性；根本性」

senses.title: Coming at the very end
senses.definition: happening or coming at the end of a long process
senses.definitionCN: 发生或出现在一个漫长过程的末尾
senses.example: The ultimate decision rests with the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 最终的决定权在委员会手里。
senses.why: Latin ultimus is the superlative of ulterior, meaning farther, so ultimate is literally the farthest point.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ultimus 是 ulterior（更远的）的最高级，因此 ultimate 字面上就是「最远的那个点」。

senses.title: Most basic and fundamental
senses.definition: being the basic cause or the power behind everything else
senses.definitionCN: 作为其他一切背后的根本原因或力量
senses.example: The ultimate cause of the failure was poor planning.
senses.exampleCN: 失败的根本原因是计划不当。
senses.why: At the farthest point you reach the bottom of things, so the last item in a chain becomes the root of it.
senses.whyCN: 走到最远的尽头就触及了事物的底，于是链条的最后一环成了它的根。

senses.title: The best or most extreme example
senses.definition: the finest or most complete example of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 同类中最好、最完整的例子
senses.example: This little car is the ultimate city vehicle.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆小车是城市用车的极致。
senses.why: Whatever stands at the far end of a scale is the extreme, and the extreme reads as perfection.
senses.whyCN: 处在刻度最远一端的即是极端，而极端常被读成完美。

senses.title: Highest in authority
senses.definition: holding the highest power, with no one above
senses.definitionCN: 掌握最高权力，其上无人
senses.example: The ultimate authority on the rules is the court.
senses.exampleCN: 规则的最终权威是法院。
senses.why: A chain of command is also a line, and the person at its far end cannot be overruled.
senses.whyCN: 指挥链也是一条线，站在最远端的人无法再被推翻。

senses.title: The finest point of something
senses.definition: the most developed state that something can reach
senses.definitionCN: 某事物所能达到的最成熟状态
senses.example: This chair is the ultimate in simple design.
senses.exampleCN: 这把椅子是简约设计的顶点。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a noun that names the far end itself.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转作名词，直接指称那条线的远端。

intro.en: The word comes straight from Latin and keeps its superlative shape.
intro.cn: 这个词直接来自拉丁语，至今保留最高级形态。

items.en: Ulter means beyond, and its comparative ulterior means farther.
items.cn: ulter 意为「在那边」，其比较级 ulterior 意为「更远的」。

items.en: Ultimus is the superlative, the farthest or last, and gives nouns such as ultimus finis, the last boundary.
items.cn: ultimus 是最高级，意为「最远的、最后的」，构成 ultimus finis（最后的边界）等说法。

items.en: Late Latin ultimatus is a participle formed on ultimus, meaning brought to the end.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 ultimatus 由 ultimus 构成的动词分词，意为「被带到尽头」。

items.en: English takes ultimate in the seventeenth century for what comes last.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 ultimate，指居于最后之物。

items.en: Modern usage adds the sense of the most extreme or finest case.
items.cn: 现代用法又添了「最极端、最出色」之义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ult- stem, and the near-meaning group gathers words about endings and extremes.
note.cn: 形近组共用 ult- 词干，近义组汇集表示结尾与极致之词。

entries.definition: a final demand backed by threats
hidden and beyond what is said

normalIntro.en: The word is the superlative of a Latin word for beyond, so it always carries the picture of a far end.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「更远」一词的最高级，因此总带着「最远端」的画面。

normal.en: Ultimus is the Latin superlative for farthest, and -ate marks it as an adjective in English.
normal.cn: ultimus 是拉丁语「最远」的最高级，-ate 让它成为英语形容词。

normal.en: Ultimately is the adverb and means in the end or at bottom.
normal.cn: ultimately 是副词，意为最终、说到底。

normal.en: An ultimatum is the last word that ends a negotiation.
normal.cn: ultimatum 是结束谈判的最后那句话。

normal.en: Ulterior motives lie beyond the surface, on the far side of what is said.
normal.cn: ulterior motives 藏在表面之外，在话语的另一边。

normal.en: The ultimate goal is the one every other step serves.
normal.cn: ultimate goal 是其他每一步都为之服务的那一个。

abstract.en: Trace a long line to its last centimetre and plant a flag there.
abstract.cn: 把一条长线画到最后一厘米，在那里插一面旗。

abstract.en: Notice that the flag also marks the deepest cause, not only the end.
abstract.cn: 注意这面旗不只标终点，也标最深的根。

abstract.en: Turn the same scale around and see everything piled up at one extreme.
abstract.cn: 再把刻度翻过来，看见一切都堆在一个顶端。

examples.en: Their ultimate aim was to make the service free.
examples.cn: 他们的最终目的是让这项服务免费。

examples.en: He is ultimately responsible for the whole team.
examples.cn: 最终要为整个团队负责的是他。

examples.en: For many cooks, this knife is the ultimate in simplicity.
examples.cn: 在很多厨师眼里，这把刀就是简约的极致。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥特妹」——奥特曼的妹妹总是站在队伍最末尾，最后一个出场。

root: 拉丁语 ulter（在那边）、比较级 ulterior（更远的）、最高级 ultimus（最远的、最后的），晚期拉丁语 ultimatus 进入英语；同族有 ultimately、ultimatum

sensesIntro.en: All senses place something at the far end of a line, whether a process, a cause, a scale, or a hierarchy.
sensesIntro.cn: 所有义项都把某物放在一条线的远端：过程的尾、原因的根、刻度的端，或等级的顶。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flag standing at the last point of a long road.
core.cn: 核心意象：长路最后一点上立着的一面旗。

branches.en: The time branch: what happens after everything else.
branches.cn: 时间分支：在其他一切之后发生的事。

branches.en: The cause branch: what lies under all the other reasons.
branches.cn: 原因分支：压在其他理由下面的那一层。

branches.en: The quality branch: the extreme example and its noun form.
branches.cn: 程度分支：极端的范例及其名词形式。

branches.en: The power branch: the top of a chain of command.
branches.cn: 权力分支：指挥链的最顶端。

branches.en: The everyday sense in which a goal or a decision comes last.
branches.cn: 日常义：目标或决定排在最后。

intro.en: The word is a Latin superlative stem dressed as an English adjective.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语最高级词干披上英语形容词外衣。

latinIntro.en: The ulter family clusters around the idea of beyond.
latinIntro.cn: ulter 这一族词都围绕「在那边」的意思。

items.example: Ultimate keeps the Latin stem as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: ultimate 以形容词身份保留拉丁词干。

items.example: An ulterior reason stays out of sight.
items.exampleCN: 别有用心的理由藏在看不见处。

items.example: They questioned the ultimacy of the rule.
items.exampleCN: 他们质疑这条规则的终极性。

definition_zh: 最终；最后；归根到底；根本上
definition_en: after everything has been considered, or in the end
core_image: 把一路的枝叶都拨开，露出最底下那句结论
scene: 两位合伙人争执了一整个下午，白板上写满了各种方案，到最后只剩一句结论。Ultimately, they agreed to sell the small factory.
sceneCN: 这里 ultimately 是「最终、归根到底」（第 1 个义项：经过全部过程之后）；句意为他们最终同意卖掉那座小工厂。拨开枝叶看见底下那句话，正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ly 的形容词，义为「最终的；根本的」
同源名词，义为「终极性」
同源名词，义为「最后通牒」

senses.title: In the end after a long process
senses.definition: after a series of events or a period of time, when everything is over
senses.definitionCN: 在一系列事件或一段时间之后，一切结束时
senses.example: The two sides ultimately reached a deal.
senses.exampleCN: 双方最终达成了协议。
senses.why: Ultimate names the farthest point, and -ly turns that point into the moment it is reached.
senses.whyCN: ultimate 指最远的那个点，-ly 把这个点变成为抵达它的那一刻。

senses.title: Fundamentally, when everything is considered
senses.definition: when all reasons are weighed, this is the real explanation
senses.definitionCN: 把所有理由都称过之后，真正的解释是这个
senses.example: Success ultimately depends on trust.
senses.exampleCN: 成功归根到底取决于信任。
senses.why: To reach the last item in a chain of reasons is to reach its foundation, so the adverb doubles as fundamentally.
senses.whyCN: 走到理由链条的最后一环就是触到地基，所以这个副词也兼有「根本上」之义。

senses.title: Used to sum up a complex account
senses.definition: used when a long explanation is being reduced to one short statement
senses.definitionCN: 用于把一大段解释压缩成一句简短的话
senses.example: It was a long quarrel, but ultimately a small one.
senses.exampleCN: 那是场很长的争吵，但说到底也是件小事。
senses.why: The far end of a story is where a summary naturally sits.
senses.whyCN: 故事的最远端，正是一段总结自然该坐的位置。

senses.title: In the final analysis of a judgement
senses.definition: used to give the final judgement on a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 用于对人或物给出最后判断
senses.example: She is ultimately a very cautious person.
senses.exampleCN: 从根本上说，她是个非常谨慎的人。
senses.why: A judgement that strips away surface detail looks at the far end of the description.
senses.whyCN: 剥掉表面细节的判断，看的是描述的最远端。

senses.title: In the long run over a lifetime or history
senses.definition: over a long stretch of time, such as a life or a period of history
senses.definitionCN: 在很长一段时间里，如一生或一段历史
senses.example: Cheap coal was ultimately a costly choice.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价煤终将被证明是昂贵的选择。
senses.why: The longest line available is time itself, and its far end is where this sense lives.
senses.whyCN: 能想到的最长的线就是时间，这个义项住在它最远的一端。

intro.en: The adverb is the adjective ultimate with the English suffix -ly added.
intro.cn: 这个副词是形容词 ultimate 加上英语后缀 -ly 构成的。

items.en: Ultimus is the superlative of ulter, beyond, and means farthest or last.
items.cn: ultimus 是 ulter（在那边）的最高级，意为最远、最后。

items.en: The stem gives Latin ultimatus, brought to an end.
items.cn: 这个词干又生出拉丁语 ultimatus，意为「被带到尽头」。

items.en: Ultimate enters English in the seventeenth century, and the adverb follows it.
items.cn: ultimate 在十七世纪进入英语，副词随后出现。

items.en: The -ly form is used early for what comes last in reasoning as well as in time.
items.cn: 加 -ly 的形式很早就同时用于时间上的最后与推理上的最后。

items.en: Modern English makes ultimately a very common summing-up word in formal writing.
items.cn: 现代英语里 ultimately 成了正式写作中常用的总结词。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the ultim- family, and the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of conclusion.
note.cn: 形近组展示 ultim- 词族，近义组汇集表示结论的副词。

entries.definition: at last, after a long time

normalIntro.en: Take the superlative adjective for farthest and add the adverb ending.
normalIntro.cn: 把表示「最远」的最高级形容词加上副词词尾即可。

normal.en: Ultimate plus -ly gives the adverb, exactly as usual and final give usually and finally.
normal.cn: ultimate 加 -ly 得副词，与 usual 变 usually、final 变 finally 同理。

normal.en: Ultimately often heads a sentence that sums up a long discussion.
normal.cn: ultimately 常领起一句话，用来总结一长段讨论。

normal.en: The word sits next to verbs of deciding, depending, and proving.
normal.cn: 这个词常与 decide、depend、prove 这类动词搭配。

normal.en: Ultimate is the adjective, ultimacy the noun of finality.
normal.cn: ultimate 是形容词，ultimacy 是表示终极性的名词。

normal.en: An ultimatum is the last word before action, the same far end.
normal.cn: ultimatum 是行动前最后那句话，同一个最远端。

abstract.en: Brush away leaves until one plain sentence lies on the ground.
abstract.cn: 把枯叶一层层拨开，直到地上只剩一句平白的话。

abstract.en: Look down the whole line of reasons to its last link.
abstract.cn: 顺着整条理由的链子望到最后一环。

abstract.en: Then step back and let the far point become one adverb.
abstract.cn: 再退后一步，让那个远点缩成一个副词。

examples.en: The project ultimately succeeded despite every setback.
examples.cn: 尽管屡遭挫折，这个项目最终还是成功了。

examples.en: What people buy is ultimately a matter of trust.
examples.cn: 人们买什么，归根到底是信任问题。

examples.en: Ultimately, the choice is yours to make.
examples.cn: 说到底，选择权在你手里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥特妹特利」——奥特妹特别利落地收尾，最后一句总是她说。

root: 形容词 ultimate（拉丁语 ultimus「最远的、最后的」）加英语副词后缀 -ly；同族有 ultimate、ultimatum、ulterior

sensesIntro.en: The adverb marks the far end of a process, a reason, a judgement, or a stretch of time.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个副词标记一条线的远端：过程、理由、判断或一段时间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the single sentence left after the leaves are brushed away.
core.cn: 核心意象：拨开枝叶后剩下的那一句话。

branches.en: The process branch: what happens once events are over.
branches.cn: 过程分支：事件结束之后发生的事。

branches.en: The root branch: the real explanation and the final judgement.
branches.cn: 根源分支：真正的解释与最后的判断。

branches.en: The summary branch: one short statement for a long story.
branches.cn: 总结分支：一段长话压成一句短话。

branches.en: The time branch: what proves true over a lifetime or an age.
branches.cn: 时间分支：在一生或一个时代里被证明为真。

branches.en: The commonest use, simply in the end.
branches.cn: 最常见的用法：不过是「最后」。

intro.en: An English adverb ending added to a Latin superlative adjective.
intro.cn: 英语副词词尾加在拉丁语最高级形容词上。

latinIntro.en: The base is the Latin superlative for farthest.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语表示「最远」的最高级。

items.example: The ultimacy of the rule is in doubt.
items.exampleCN: 这条规则的终极性存疑。
他心里另有一个隐秘的目的。

definition_zh: 雨伞；伞；保护伞；总体框架；覆盖范围
definition_en: a folding cover held over the head against rain, or a general system that includes many parts
core_image: 一朵撑开的圆顶罩在头顶，把落下的东西全挡在外面
scene: 地铁口挤满了人，雨点斜斜打进来，只有一把黑伞稳稳撑在台阶上方。She shook the rain off her umbrella and stepped inside.
sceneCN: 这里 umbrella 是「雨伞」（第 1 个义项：挡雨的伞）；句意为她抖掉伞上的雨水走了进来。头顶那朵撑开的圆顶正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 复合形容词，义为「伞状的」
名词加 -ed 构成，义为「被伞覆盖的」
同源名词，义为「阴影；本影」

senses.title: A cover held against rain
senses.definition: a light folding frame with cloth over it, held above the head to keep off rain
senses.definitionCN: 轻便的折叠骨架蒙上布，撑在头顶挡雨
senses.example: He forgot his umbrella and got soaked.
senses.exampleCN: 他忘了带伞，浑身湿透。
senses.why: Latin umbra means shade, and its diminutive umbrella is a little shade carried in the hand.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 umbra 意为阴影，其指小形式 umbrellas 就是一顶拿在手里的「小阴影」。

senses.title: A cover against sun
senses.definition: a similar cover used for shade from strong sun
senses.definitionCN: 用途相同的伞，用来遮住强烈的阳光
senses.example: A striped umbrella stood over the cafe table.
senses.exampleCN: 咖啡桌上撑着条纹的遮阳伞。
senses.why: The first purpose was shade, so the sun sense is the older one.
senses.whyCN: 最初的功能就是遮阳，所以遮阳义反而更古老。

senses.title: A protective system or power
senses.definition: something powerful that shelters those under it from harm
senses.definitionCN: 某种强大的力量，在其下者可以免于伤害
senses.example: The small state sheltered under the umbrella of its ally.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小国躲在盟友的保护伞下。
senses.why: A cover above your head becomes a metaphor for a power that shields a whole group.
senses.whyCN: 头顶的遮盖转成了比喻，指遮护一整群人的力量。

senses.title: A general framework covering many parts
senses.definition: an arrangement or body that includes several smaller groups
senses.definitionCN: 把若干较小团体包含在内的一套安排或机构
senses.example: The two labs work under one umbrella.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个实验室共处一个总框架之下。
senses.why: One dome over many heads becomes one system over many units.
senses.whyCN: 一顶圆顶罩住许多人的头，就成了一套系统罩住许多单位。

senses.title: A word or term that covers many kinds
senses.definition: a word used to name a whole category of related things
senses.definitionCN: 用来命名一整类相关事物的词
senses.example: Fruit is an umbrella term that hides a lot of variety.
senses.exampleCN: fruit 是个总称，底下藏着极大的多样。
senses.why: A label that spreads over its members works exactly like a dome over people.
senses.whyCN: 一个摊开覆盖成员的标签，作用正像罩住人群的圆顶。

intro.en: The word is a small Latin shade that travelled through Italian into English.
intro.cn: 这个词是一顶拉丁语的「小阴影」，经意大利语传入英语。

items.en: Umbra means shade or shadow, and umbraculum is a shade or a sunshade.
items.cn: umbra 意为阴影，umbraculum 是遮荫处或阳伞。

items.en: The diminutive ending -ella is added in medieval Italian forms, giving a little shade.
items.cn: 指小词尾 -ella 出现在中世纪意大利语形式里，形成「小阴影」。

items.en: Italian umbrella and its variants name a parasol carried against the sun.
items.cn: 意大利语中的相关形式指手持的遮阳伞。

items.en: English borrows umbrella in the seventeenth century from Italian, then moves it from sun to rain.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪从意大利语借入，随后把它从遮阳转向挡雨。

items.en: Modern English extends it to political protection and to general frameworks.
items.cn: 现代英语又把它扩展到政治保护与总体框架。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers umbr- words about shade, and the near-meaning group collects covers and frameworks.
note.cn: 形近组汇集带 umbr- 的「阴影」词，近义组汇集遮盖与框架类词。

entries.definition: the darkest part of a shadow
a wide-brimmed hat that gives shade
a light umbrella for the sun
a canvas sheet over a doorway
a basic structure holding parts together

normalIntro.en: The word is literally a small shade, since Latin umbra is the shadow a dome casts.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词字面上就是「小阴影」，因为拉丁语 umbra 正是圆顶投下的影。

normal.en: Umbra is Latin for shade, and umbrella is a portable shade on a stick.
normal.cn: umbra 是拉丁语的阴影，umbrella 就是装在柄上的随身小阴影。

normal.en: Umbrella organization uses the dome as an image for one body over many.
normal.cn: umbrella organization 把圆顶用作一个机构罩住许多单位的意象。

normal.en: Under the umbrella of is a frequent phrase in politics and law.
normal.cn: under the umbrella of 是政治与法律文本里的高频短语。

normal.en: Parasol and umbra belong to the same family of shade words.
normal.cn: parasol 与拉丁词根 umbra 同属「遮影」词族。

normal.en: The plural is simply umbrellas, with no doubling of a letter.
normal.cn: 复数直接加 s 作 umbrellas，字母不双写。

abstract.en: See a black dome open above a crowded doorway.
abstract.cn: 看见一顶黑圆顶在拥挤的门口撑开。

abstract.en: Watch the rain slide off its edge in a ring.
abstract.cn: 看雨水沿着边缘滑成一圈。

abstract.en: Then widen that dome until it covers a whole industry.
abstract.cn: 再把那圆顶撑大，直到它盖住整个行业。

examples.en: Take an umbrella, the forecast is bad.
examples.cn: 带把伞吧，天气预报不好。

examples.en: These small groups all sit under the umbrella of one charity.
examples.cn: 这些小团体都归在一家慈善机构之下。

examples.en: The umbrella stand by the door was full of dripping black canes.
examples.cn: 门边的伞架里插满了滴水的黑伞柄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺不来了」——外面下着雨，俺不来了，除非你给我一把伞。

root: 拉丁语 umbra（阴影）+ 指小后缀 -ella，经意大利语 umbrella 传入英语；同族有 umbra、umbrage、parasol

sensesIntro.en: Every sense keeps the dome image: something round spreads above and shelters what lies beneath it.
sensesIntro.cn: 每个义项都保留圆顶意象：一片圆盖在上方铺开，遮住下面的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open dome held above the head against what falls.
core.cn: 核心意象：撑在头顶挡落物的圆顶。

branches.en: The physical branch: one against rain, one against sun.
branches.cn: 实物分支：一把挡雨，一把遮阳。

branches.en: The protection branch, where power plays the part of the dome.
branches.cn: 保护分支：权力扮演圆顶的角色。

branches.en: The structure branch, one body over many units.
branches.cn: 结构分支：一个机构罩住许多单位。

branches.en: The language branch, one word over many kinds.
branches.cn: 语言分支：一个词罩住许多类别。

branches.en: The ordinary sense a rainy morning brings to mind.
branches.cn: 下雨的早晨最先想到的普通义项。

intro.en: A Latin shade root plus a little-ending, borrowed through Italian.
intro.cn: 拉丁语「阴影」词根加指小词尾，经意大利语借入。

latinIntro.en: The umbra root covers shadow in both Latin and modern science.
latinIntro.cn: umbra 词根在拉丁语和现代科学里都指阴影。

items.example: Umbra names the darkest part of a shadow.
items.exampleCN: umbra 指影子最暗的部分。

items.example: The ending makes a little shade.

items.exampleCN: 他们组成了一个总机构。

items.example: He took umbrage at the remark.

items.exampleCN: 一把遮阳伞为桌子遮荫。

definition_zh: 不能的；不会的；无能力的；不能胜任的
definition_en: not having the ability, means, or chance to do something
core_image: 伸手去够，指尖却在半空停住
scene: 病房里，老人试着抬高手臂去够水杯，手指抖了几下还是落在床单上。After the operation he was unable to walk without help.
sceneCN: 这里 unable 是「不能、无法」（第 1 个义项：没有能力做某事）；句意为手术后他无法自己走路。伸出的手停在半空，正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 同义名词，义为「无能力；不能」
加前缀 en- 构成的动词，义为「使能够」
较少用的形容词，义为「无能力的」（多见于旧文本）

senses.title: Not having the ability to do something
senses.definition: not having the power, skill, or strength to do something
senses.definitionCN: 没有能力、技能或力气去做某事
senses.example: She was unable to lift the box alone.
senses.exampleCN: 她一个人搬不动那个箱子。
senses.why: The prefix un- reverses able, and able itself comes from Latin habilis, easy to hold, so unable means not up to the task.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 反转 able，而 able 源自拉丁语 habilis（易于把握），所以 unable 就是「拿不下这件活」。

senses.title: Prevented by circumstances
senses.definition: not in a position to do something because of rules, time, or events
senses.definitionCN: 因规定、时间或事件而不处于能做的位置
senses.example: We were unable to answer before the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 截止前我们没能答复。
senses.why: If the hand is there but the door is locked, the word still applies, since the act cannot be completed.
senses.whyCN: 手是伸得出来的，但门锁着，这个动作完成不了，词照样适用。

senses.title: Lacking the strength or health
senses.definition: too weak or ill to carry out an action
senses.definitionCN: 虚弱或生病以致做不了某个动作
senses.example: He is still unable to speak after the stroke.
senses.exampleCN: 中风之后他仍然说不出话。
senses.why: Bodily strength is the oldest kind of ability, so its loss is the clearest case of unable.
senses.whyCN: 身体的力量是最古老的一种能力，失去它最能说明 unable。

senses.title: Not qualified or competent
senses.definition: not competent enough for a task or office
senses.definitionCN: 能力不足以担当某项职责
senses.example: The board found him unable to run the firm.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会认为他无力经营这家公司。
senses.why: From one failed action the word widens to a standing judgement on a person.
senses.whyCN: 从一次做不成，这个词扩展到对一个人的总体评定。

senses.title: Not permitted under a rule
senses.definition: not allowed by law or rule to do something
senses.definitionCN: 依法律或规则不被允许做某事
senses.example: Jurors are unable to discuss the case outside court.
senses.exampleCN: 陪审员在庭外不得讨论此案。
senses.why: When a rule removes the power, the person is formally unable even if capable.
senses.whyCN: 规则一旦抽走权力，即便人有本事，在形式上也是 unable。

intro.en: The word is a simple English negative of able, itself borrowed from Latin.
intro.cn: 这个词是 able 的英语否定形式，而 able 本身借自拉丁语。

items.en: Habilis means handy or easy to handle, from habere, to hold.
items.cn: habilis 意为「顺手的、易于把握的」，源自 habere（持有）。

items.en: Old French able or hable carries the sense of fit and capable into English.
items.cn: 古法语 able（或 hable）把「合适、有能力」之义带进英语。

items.en: English able appears in the fourteenth century with the sense of suited to an action.
items.cn: 英语 able 在十四世纪出现，意为「适合做某事」。

items.en: The prefix un- is added to make the negative, a regular English pattern.
items.cn: 加上前缀 un- 构成否定，这是英语的常规构词法。

items.en: Modern usage favors be unable to over cannot in formal and official writing.
items.cn: 现代正式与公文写作偏爱 be unable to，而非 cannot。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the able family, and the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of lacking power.
note.cn: 形近组展示 able 词族，近义组汇集表示缺乏能力的形容词。

entries.definition: having the power to do something
to take away the power to act
without the means to act alone
having no power to change things
having the ability to do something

normalIntro.en: Un- says no, and able says fit for the job, so the whole word is a plain refusal.
normalIntro.cn: un- 表示否定，able 表示「胜任」，合起来就是一记朴素的拒绝。

normal.en: Able comes from Latin habilis, easy to hold, so unable means the thing will not be held.
normal.cn: able 源自拉丁语 habilis（易于把握），unable 意即「把那东西握不住」。

normal.en: Enable adds en- and means to give the power; disable takes it away.
normal.cn: enable 加 en- 意为授予能力；disable 意为夺走能力。

normal.en: Inability is the matching noun, used for a general lack of power.
normal.cn: inability 是对应的名词，指总体上的无能。

normal.en: Formal writing prefers be unable to where speech would say cannot.
normal.cn: 正式写作偏好 be unable to，口语则多用 cannot。

normal.en: Unable is followed by to plus a verb, never by a bare verb.
normal.cn: unable 后面接 to 加动词，不能直接接动词原形。

abstract.en: Reach for a glass and watch your fingers stop in the air.
abstract.cn: 伸手去够杯子，看手指在半空停下。

abstract.en: Feel the strength drain from the arm while the wish stays.
abstract.cn: 感觉力气从手臂流走，而愿望还在。

abstract.en: Then hear a rule close the door even though your hand is free.
abstract.cn: 再听一条规则把门关上，哪怕你的手是自由的。

examples.en: He was unable to attend the meeting because of the storm.
examples.cn: 因为暴风雨，他没能出席会议。

examples.en: The little girl was unable to reach the top shelf.
examples.cn: 小女孩够不到最上面那层架子。

examples.en: Witnesses are unable to comment while the case is open.
examples.cn: 案件审理期间证人不得置评。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺能波」——俺的能力像水面上的波，一伸手就散了。

root: un-（否定前缀）+ able（拉丁语 habilis「易于把握的」，源自动词 habere「持有」）；同族有 enable、disable、ability

sensesIntro.en: The single idea is a hand that cannot close on the thing it wants, whether for strength, circumstance, or rule.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心只有一个意思：那只手合不上想要的东西，无论原因是力气、处境还是规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a reaching hand that stops short in the air.
core.cn: 核心意象：伸出的手在半空停住。

branches.en: The ability branch: skill and bodily strength that fall short.
branches.cn: 能力分支：技巧与体力不够。

branches.en: The circumstance branch, where time or events block the act.
branches.cn: 处境分支：时间或事件挡住了行动。

branches.en: The competence branch, a standing judgement on a person.
branches.cn: 胜任分支：对一个人的总体评定。

branches.en: The rule branch, where permission is withdrawn.
branches.cn: 规则分支：许可被抽走。

branches.en: The plain everyday sense, the one closest to the hand image.
branches.cn: 最日常的义项，也最贴近那只手的画面。

intro.en: A negation prefix over a Latin word for what can be handled.
intro.cn: 否定前缀盖在一个表示「能把得住」的拉丁词上。

latinIntro.en: The able root goes back to Latin habere, to hold.
latinIntro.cn: able 的词根可追到拉丁语 habere（持有）。

items.exampleCN: unable 就是 able 的否定。

items.example: She is able to help today.

items.exampleCN: 这把钥匙让人能够进入。
光线太差让相机无法工作。

items.example: His inability to swim worried them.
items.exampleCN: 他不会游泳让他们担心。

items.example: Able and unable take -ness in older prose.
items.exampleCN: able 与 unable 在旧式散文里可加 -ness。

definition_zh: 不能接受的；难以忍受的；不合格的；令人不满的
definition_en: not good enough to be agreed to, tolerated, or let through
core_image: 一件东西递到门口，被守门人抬手推了回去
scene: 会议室的门口贴着一张告示，写着着装要求，短裤和拖鞋一律不许进。Loud phone calls during the lecture are simply unacceptable.
sceneCN: 这里 unacceptable 是「不能接受的」（第 1 个义项：不足以让人同意或容许）；句意为在讲座中大声打电话简直不可接受。递来的东西被守门人推回，正是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 形容词：不能接受的；不可容许的
形容词：不合格的；难以忍受的

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「不可接受地」
形容词加 -ability 构成名词，义为「不可接受性」
去掉否定前缀的原动词，义为「接受」

senses.title: Not able to be agreed to
senses.definition: so poor or wrong that no one can agree to it
senses.definitionCN: 太差或太错，以致无人能同意
senses.example: The terms were unacceptable to both sides.
senses.exampleCN: 这些条件双方都无法接受。
senses.why: Accept comes from Latin accipere, to receive, so unacceptable describes something the hand refuses to take.
senses.whyCN: accept 来自拉丁语 accipere（接收），因此 unacceptable 就是「拒绝接过来的东西」。

senses.title: Not to be tolerated
senses.definition: behaving in a way that a community will not put up with
senses.definitionCN: 行为方式让所在群体无法容忍
senses.example: Such rude remarks are unacceptable here.
senses.exampleCN: 这种粗鲁的话在这里是不可容忍的。
senses.why: To tolerate is to bear a weight, and what a community will not bear is by definition unacceptable.
senses.whyCN: tolerate 意为承重，一个群体不肯承起的东西，按定义就是 unacceptable。

senses.title: Below the required standard
senses.definition: falling short of the standard set for a product or a piece of work
senses.definitionCN: 未达到产品或作品所设定的标准
senses.example: The water sample was unacceptable for drinking.
senses.exampleCN: 这个水样不适合饮用。
senses.why: A receiver turns away what fails inspection, and the same word covers goods and grades.
senses.whyCN: 收货人会把检验不合格的东西退回，同一个词也覆盖货物与成绩。

senses.title: Too great to bear
senses.definition: of a risk or cost, too high to be allowed to stand
senses.definitionCN: 就风险或代价而言高到不允许存在
senses.example: The delay posed an unacceptable risk to patients.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误给病人带来了不可承受的风险。
senses.why: From a thing you will not take, the word moves to a level you will not let stand.
senses.whyCN: 从「不肯接下的东西」转到「不肯让它继续存在的程度」。

senses.title: Morally or socially offensive
senses.titleCN: 令人难以接受的；有伤风化的
senses.definition: offending the moral sense of most people
senses.definitionCN: 冒犯多数人的道德感
senses.example: The film was criticized for its unacceptable portrayal of violence.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影因对暴力的呈现令人难以接受而受到批评。
senses.why: A whole society can refuse a portrayal just as a person refuses a parcel.
senses.whyCN: 整个社会也可以像个人拒收包裹那样，拒绝一种呈现方式。

intro.en: The word is the English negative of acceptable, which comes from Latin.
intro.cn: 这个词是 acceptable 的英语否定形式，后者来自拉丁语。

items.en: Accipere joins ad-, to, and capere, to take, meaning to receive.
items.cn: accipere 由 ad-（向）与 capere（拿）组成，意为接收。

items.en: Acceptabilis is what is welcome or pleasing when received.
items.cn: acceptabilis 指接到手时令人满意的、受欢迎的东西。

items.en: Old French passes acceptable into English with the same sense of welcome.
items.cn: 古法语把 acceptable 传入英语，仍含「受欢迎」之义。

items.en: The un- negative appears as the word spreads into contracts and rules.
items.cn: 随着这个词进入契约与规则文本，un- 否定形出现了。

items.en: Modern usage makes it a standard phrase of complaint and of policy.
items.cn: 现代用法让它成为抱怨与政策文本中的常用词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the accept family, and the near-meaning group collects words of refusal and fault.
note.cn: 形近组汇集 accept 词族，近义组汇集表示拒绝与不合格的词。

entries.definition: good enough to be agreed to
the act of receiving or agreeing
not yet received or agreed to

normalIntro.en: Read it as a hand at the door: un- says no, accept says take, able says can be.
normalIntro.cn: 把它读成门口的一只手：un- 说不，accept 说接，able 说能。

normal.en: Accept comes from capere, to take, so unacceptable is what will not be taken.
normal.cn: accept 源自 capere（拿），unacceptable 就是拿不下、不肯接的。

normal.en: Acceptable and unacceptable pair up as the two verdicts on a proposal.
normal.cn: acceptable 与 unacceptable 是一对判词，用来评价一项提议。

normal.en: Acceptance is the noun for taking something in; unacceptability is the quality of being refused.
normal.cn: acceptance 是接纳这一行为的名词，unacceptability 是被拒的性质。

normal.en: The adverb unacceptably often stands before high, slow, or long.
normal.cn: 副词 unacceptably 常放在 high、slow、long 前。

normal.en: Contracts use it for terms, and doctors use it for risk levels.
normal.cn: 契约里用它说条款，医生用它说风险等级。

abstract.en: See a parcel pushed back across a counter without a word.
abstract.cn: 看见一个包裹被无声地推回柜台外面。

abstract.en: Watch a doorman raise one flat palm at a badly dressed guest.
abstract.cn: 看门卫对一位穿着不当的客人竖起手掌。

abstract.en: Then feel a number on a gauge climb past the red line.
abstract.cn: 再感觉仪表上的数字爬过红线。

examples.en: The committee found the proposal unacceptable.
examples.cn: 委员会认为这项提议不可接受。

examples.en: Cheating is unacceptable in any competition.
examples.cn: 任何竞赛中作弊都是不可接受的。

examples.en: The noise level at night was unacceptably high.
examples.cn: 夜里的噪声水平高得让人无法接受。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺不能赛普特波」——这样的东西俺不接受，也别塞破布来凑数。

root: un-（否定前缀）+ acceptable（拉丁语 accipere「接收」，由 ad-「向」+ capere「拿」构成）

sensesIntro.en: All senses refuse something: a term, a behaviour, a product, a risk, or a portrayal.
sensesIntro.cn: 所有义项都在拒绝某物：条款、行为、产品、风险或一种描绘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a parcel pushed back across the counter.
core.cn: 核心意象：包裹被推回柜台外。

branches.en: The negotiation branch, where a term cannot be agreed.
branches.cn: 谈判分支：条款无法被同意。

branches.en: The conduct branch, where behaviour offends the community.
branches.cn: 行为分支：行为冒犯了群体。

branches.en: The quality branch, where a product fails the standard.
branches.cn: 质量分支：产品不达标准。

branches.en: The risk branch, where a level is too high to allow.
branches.cn: 风险分支：程度高到不能允许。

branches.en: The plain sense used in everyday complaint.
branches.cn: 日常抱怨里最常用的朴素义项。

intro.en: A negation prefix, a taking verb, and an ability ending stacked together.
intro.cn: 否定前缀、表示「拿」的动词、表示「可以」的词尾叠在一起。

latinIntro.en: The capere root, to take, also lies behind capture, receive, and except.
latinIntro.cn: capere（拿）这一词根还支撑着 capture、receive、except 等词。

items.example: Accipere begins with a movement toward.
items.exampleCN: accipere 开头的部分表示朝对方移动。
capere 支撑着 capture 与 receive。
除他之外所有人都同意。

definition_zh: 不确定的；无把握的；无法确定的；无常的；犹豫的
definition_en: not sure or not known, and therefore liable to change
core_image: 雾里的一条岔路，看不清哪一条通向哪里
scene: 出发前夜，一家人围着地图讨论路线，天气预报却每小时都在改。The date of the wedding is still uncertain.
sceneCN: 这里 uncertain 是「不确定的、未定的」（第 1 个义项：不能确定是否或何时）；句意为婚礼的日期还没定下来。雾中岔路看不清，正是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 形容词：不确定的；无把握的
形容词：变化无常的；靠不住的

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ty 构成名词，义为「不确定性；疑虑」
形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「不肯定地；迟疑地」
去掉否定前缀的原词，义为「确定的」

senses.title: Not known for sure
senses.definition: not established as a fact, and so open to doubt
senses.definitionCN: 尚未确定成为事实，因此存疑
senses.example: The cause of the fire is still uncertain.
senses.exampleCN: 起火原因仍未确定。
senses.why: Certain comes from Latin certus, settled, so uncertain is what has not been settled.
senses.whyCN: certain 源自拉丁语 certus（已定的），uncertain 就是「尚未被定下来的」。

senses.title: Not confident in one’s own mind
senses.definition: feeling doubt about one’s knowledge or judgement
senses.definitionCN: 对自己的知识或判断感到怀疑
senses.example: I am uncertain about the wording of the rule.
senses.exampleCN: 我对这条规则的确切措辞没有把握。
senses.why: When the fact is not settled, the mind that holds it also cannot settle.
senses.whyCN: 事实没有落定，心里装着它的人也落定不了。

senses.title: Likely to change and unreliable
senses.definition: unsteady, and likely to shift without warning
senses.definitionCN: 不稳定，随时可能无预警地改变
senses.example: This region has uncertain rainfall.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区的降雨很不稳定。
senses.why: Details that are not fixed produce conditions that cannot be trusted.
senses.whyCN: 没有定下来的细节，造出不能信赖的状况。

senses.title: Hesitant in movement or manner
senses.definition: moving or speaking in a way that shows doubt
senses.definitionCN: 动作或说话显出犹疑
senses.example: He took an uncertain step toward the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他迟疑地朝门口迈了一步。
senses.why: The body copies the mind: a doubtful thought produces a hesitant step.
senses.whyCN: 身体会照着心走：犹豫的念头生犹疑的脚步。

senses.title: Not definitely good or bad
senses.definition: of an outcome, still open to either result
senses.definitionCN: 就结果而言，两种可能都还在
senses.example: The election result remains uncertain.
senses.exampleCN: 选举结果仍未可知。
senses.why: An open path with fog on it has not yet shown which way it leads.
senses.whyCN: 一条起雾的岔路，还没显出它通向哪边。

intro.en: The word is an English negative built on a Latin adjective of settled fact.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语否定形式，建在一个表示「已定事实」的拉丁形容词上。

items.en: Certus means sure, settled, or decided, from cernere, to sift and decide.
items.cn: certus 意为确定的、已定的，源自 cernere（筛选、判定）。

items.en: Old French certain carries the adjective into English with the sense of assured.
items.cn: 古法语 certain 把这个形容词带入英语，意为「保证的」。

items.en: English uses certain for what is firmly known, especially in the phrase for certain.
items.cn: 英语用 certain 指确实知道的事，尤见于 for certain 一语。

items.en: Un- is added to form the negative from the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 十四世纪起加 un- 构成否定。

items.en: The idiom in no uncertain terms keeps the negated form for emphasis.
items.cn: 习语 in no uncertain terms 用否定形式来加强语气。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the cert- family, and the near-meaning group gathers words of doubt.
note.cn: 形近组展示 cert- 词族，近义组汇集表示怀疑的词。

entries.definition: to state officially that something is true

normalIntro.en: Certus in Latin means sifted and settled, and the prefix simply takes that away.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语 certus 意为筛过、定下，前缀只是把它拿走。

normal.en: Certus comes from cernere, to sift, so an uncertain fact has not been sifted out yet.
normal.cn: certus 源自 cernere（筛拣），uncertain 的事实还没被筛清。

normal.en: Certainty and uncertainty are the two nouns, one settled and one not.
normal.cn: certainty 与 uncertainty 是两枚名词，一个已定，一个未定。

normal.en: In no uncertain terms is the fixed idiom meaning very clearly.
normal.cn: in no uncertain terms 是固定习语，意为非常明确地。

normal.en: Uncertainty is uncountable in general use but takes -ies for particular doubts.
normal.cn: uncertainty 泛指时不可数，说具体的疑虑时可用复数 uncertainties。

normal.en: Uncertain usually leads to about, as in uncertain about the details.
normal.cn: uncertain 常跟 about 搭配，如 uncertain about the details。

abstract.en: Stand where one road splits in fog and both branches fade.
abstract.cn: 站在雾里岔路口，两条岔路都渐渐淡掉。

abstract.en: Hold a coin before it lands, both sides still possible.
abstract.cn: 捏着一枚将落未落的硬币，两面都还成立。

abstract.en: Feel your own foot lift with no certainty where it will fall.
abstract.cn: 感觉自己的脚抬起来，却不知会落在哪里。

examples.en: Her tone was polite but uncertain.
examples.cn: 她的语气客气却没有把握。

examples.en: It is uncertain whether the match will be played tomorrow.
examples.cn: 明天是否比赛还不确定。

examples.en: He left in no uncertain terms that he disagreed.
examples.cn: 他非常明确地表示自己不同意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安色疼」——心上不踏实，像针扎一样隐隐作疼。

root: un-（否定前缀）+ certain（拉丁语 certus「确定的」，源自 cernere「筛拣、判定」）；同族有 certainty、certainly、certify

sensesIntro.en: Each sense is a piece of fog: an unknown fact, a doubtful mind, unsteady conditions, hesitant movement, an open result.
sensesIntro.cn: 每个义项都是一片雾：未知的事实、没底的心里、不稳的条件、迟疑的动作、未定的结果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a forked road disappearing into fog.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条岔路消失在雾里。

branches.en: The fact branch: what is not known and what has not been decided.
branches.cn: 事实分支：不知道的与未决定的。

branches.en: The mind branch: confidence that has not formed.
branches.cn: 心理分支：尚未形成的把握。

branches.en: The condition branch: weather and figures that shift.
branches.cn: 状况分支：会变动的天气与数字。

branches.en: The manner branch: a step or a voice full of doubt.
branches.cn: 方式分支：充满疑虑的脚步或嗓音。

branches.en: The plain sense used about dates and causes.
branches.cn: 谈论日期与原因时最常用的义项。

intro.en: A negation prefix over a Latin word meaning sifted and settled.
intro.cn: 否定前缀盖在「筛过、定下」的拉丁词上。

latinIntro.en: The cern- root also yields discern, decide, and discriminate.
latinIntro.cn: cern- 词根还生出 discern、decide、discriminate。

items.exampleCN: cernere 支撑着 decide 与 discern。

items.example: Certain keeps the Latin ending in English dress.
items.exampleCN: certain 以英语外衣保留拉丁语词尾。

definition_zh: 叔叔；伯伯；舅舅；姑父；姨父；（口语）大叔
definition_en: the brother of one’s father or mother, or the husband of an aunt
core_image: 饭桌旁那位总爱给你夹菜、跟父母同辈的男子
scene: 过年时家里人挤满一张大圆桌，坐在孩子旁边的那位笑眯眯地往他碗里添了一块鱼。My uncle taught me how to ride a bicycle.
sceneCN: 这里 uncle 是「舅舅或叔叔」（第 1 个义项：父或母的兄弟）；句意为叔叔教会了我骑自行车。饭桌旁给你夹菜的那位长辈正是这个词的画面。

collocations.zh: 汤姆叔叔（亦指谄媚白人者）

derivatives.zh: 对应词，义为「姑妈；姨妈；婶婶」
源自拉丁语同义词，义为「像叔伯般慈爱的」
复合名词，义为「叔伯关系的姻亲」

senses.title: Brother of one’s parent
senses.definition: the brother of your mother or your father
senses.definitionCN: 父亲或母亲的兄弟
senses.example: My uncle lives in the next town.
senses.exampleCN: 我叔叔住在邻镇。
senses.why: The word comes from Latin avunculus, a mother’s brother, which is itself a diminutive of avus, grandfather.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自拉丁语 avunculus（舅父），而 avunculus 本身是 avus（祖父）的指小形式。

senses.title: Husband of one’s aunt
senses.definition: the husband of your aunt, without blood relation
senses.definitionCN: 姑妈或姨妈的丈夫，与其无血缘关系
senses.example: Her uncle drove us to the station.
senses.exampleCN: 她姨父开车送我们去车站。
senses.why: Once a term marks a position at the family table, it covers whoever sits there by marriage.
senses.whyCN: 一旦一个词标记的是家庭餐桌上的位置，坐在那里的人无论因何而来都会被它覆盖。

senses.title: An older man addressed informally
senses.definition: a friendly form of address to a much older man
senses.definitionCN: 对年长许多的男子表示亲近的称呼
senses.example: The uncle at the night stall sold us warm buns.
senses.exampleCN: 夜市摊上的大叔卖给我们热包子。
senses.why: A family kinship word stretches into a polite warmth for strangers of the older generation.
senses.whyCN: 亲族称谓延伸到对陌生长辈的一种亲切礼貌。

senses.title: A relative of an earlier generation more generally
senses.definition: any male relative of your parents’ generation in a wide family
senses.definitionCN: 大家族中父母一辈的男性亲长
senses.example: In that village every older man is called uncle.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个村子里，年长的男人都被叫作叔叔。
senses.why: Kin terms spread outward along the ring of the family until the whole generation is covered.
senses.whyCN: 亲族称谓沿着家族的圆圈向外铺开，直到覆满整个辈分。

senses.title: Used in slang for surrender
senses.definition: in North American speech, to admit defeat by saying the word
senses.definitionCN: 在北美口语中，说一声 uncle 表示认输
senses.example: The small boy twisted away and cried uncle.
senses.exampleCN: 小男孩挣脱开，喊了声「服了」。
senses.why: A familiar name used under pressure turns into a signal of giving up.
senses.whyCN: 一个亲昵的称呼在受压制时，被转成投降的信号。

intro.en: The word goes back through French to a Latin diminutive of grandfather.
intro.cn: 这个词经法语上溯到拉丁语中「祖父」的指小形式。

items.en: Avus means grandfather, and avunculus is a little grandfather, that is the mother’s brother.
items.cn: avus 意为祖父，avunculus 就是「小祖父」，即舅父。

items.en: Old French oncle shortens and reshapes the Latin word.
items.cn: 古法语 oncle 把拉丁词缩短并改了形。

items.en: English borrows uncle around the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪前后借入 uncle。

items.en: The sense widens to cover the husband of an aunt and then older men in general.
items.cn: 词义扩大到姑父、姨父，进而泛指年长男子。

items.en: The North American idiom say uncle keeps the word inside children’s games.
items.cn: 北美习语 say uncle 让这个词留在儿童游戏里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers kin words that look and sound similar, and the near-meaning group collects family terms.
note.cn: 形近组收集形音相近的亲属词，近义组收集家庭称谓。

entries.definition: a corner or a way of looking at something
entries.definitionCN: 角；角度（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: the joint between the leg and the foot
entries.definitionCN: 脚踝（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: the son of your brother or sister
the child of your aunt or uncle

normalIntro.en: The Latin original means little grandfather, which explains why the word feels old and fond at once.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁原词意为「小祖父」，这解释了它为什么既显年长又带亲昵。

normal.en: Avunculus was the mother’s brother, the little grandfather of a household.
normal.cn: avunculus 是舅父，家里的「小祖父」。

normal.en: Aunt is the matching word on the female side, and the pair are learned together.
normal.cn: aunt 是与之配套的阴性词，两个词常一起记。

normal.en: Avuncular is the adjective for an uncle-like manner, gentle and slightly teasing.
normal.cn: avuncular 是形容叔伯作风的形容词，温和又略带打趣。

normal.en: Say uncle is the North American signal of surrender in a wrestle.
normal.cn: say uncle 是北美口语里角力时认输的信号。

normal.en: The plural is regular: uncles, with no change of the stem.
normal.cn: 复数规则变化作 uncles，词干不变。

abstract.en: See a round dinner table with one man leaning to fill a child’s bowl.
abstract.cn: 看见一张圆饭桌，一位男子俯身为孩子添饭。

abstract.en: Hear your own childhood name called by a voice one generation lower.
abstract.cn: 听见比你高一辈的声音喊你的小名。

abstract.en: Then pass the same warmth to an older stranger at a night stall.
abstract.cn: 再把同样的亲切递给夜市摊上一位年长陌生人。

examples.en: My uncle fixed the leak in the roof last Sunday.
examples.cn: 上星期天我叔叔修好了屋顶的漏水。

examples.en: She has three uncles on her mother’s side.
examples.cn: 她母亲那边有三个舅舅。

examples.en: The two brothers wrestled until the smaller one said uncle.
examples.cn: 两兄弟扭打了很久，直到小的那个喊了声服了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安口」——叔叔一进门就先安顿好你的嘴，总往你嘴里塞吃的。

root: 拉丁语 avus（祖父）的指小形式 avunculus（舅父），经古法语 oncle 进入英语；同族有 aunt、avuncular

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as the mother’s brother and widens along the family’s older generation until any warm older man can be called it.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从舅父开始，沿家族的上一个辈分不断扩大，直到任何亲切的年长男子都能用它。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the man beside the child at the family table.
core.cn: 核心意象：家庭餐桌旁坐在孩子身边的那位男子。

branches.en: The blood branch: brothers of either parent.
branches.cn: 血缘分支：父母双方的兄弟。

branches.en: The marriage branch, where an aunt’s husband joins in.
branches.cn: 婚姻分支：姑父、姨父被纳入。

branches.en: The widened branch: any older man of the parents’ generation.
branches.cn: 扩展分支：父母一辈的任何年长男子。

branches.en: The slang branch, where a kinship word means surrender.
branches.cn: 俚语分支：亲族称谓转作认输。

branches.en: The plain kinship sense used every day.
branches.cn: 日常使用的朴素亲属义。

intro.en: The word keeps the shape of a Latin diminutive rather than any English pieces.
intro.cn: 这个词保留的是拉丁语指小形式的形状，而非任何英语部件。

latinIntro.en: Avus and its little form avunculus anchor the family.
latinIntro.cn: avus 及其指小形式 avunculus 是这个词族的地基。

items.example: Avus sits at the root of uncle.
items.exampleCN: avus 是 uncle 词根的源头。
他以长辈般的口气给了建议。

items.meaning: child of an aunt or uncle

definition_zh: 不舒服的；不自在的；令人不适的；尴尬的
definition_en: not at ease in the body or the mind, or making others feel uneasy
core_image: 坐在一条太硬的板凳上，怎么挪动都硌人
scene: 长途汽车上空调坏了，座位又窄，乘客们不断换着姿势，谁也睡不踏实。The old wooden bench was hard and uncomfortable.
sceneCN: 这里 uncomfortable 是「不舒服的」（第 1 个义项：身体上不舒服）；句意为那条旧木凳又硬又不舒服。在硬板凳上怎么挪都硌人，正是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 形容词：不舒服的；不适的
形容词：不自在的；尴尬的

derivatives.zh: 去掉否定前缀的原词，义为「舒适的」
形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「不舒服地；尴尬地」
同源名词，义为「不适；不安」

senses.title: Not physically at ease
senses.definition: causing or feeling mild physical pain or stiffness
senses.definitionCN: 引起或感到轻微的身体疼痛与僵硬
senses.example: These new shoes are uncomfortable on long walks.
senses.exampleCN: 这双新鞋走远路很不舒服。
senses.why: Comfort comes from Latin confortare, to strengthen, and un- removes that ease.
senses.whyCN: comfort 源自拉丁语 confortare（使强健），un- 把这层舒服抽走。

senses.title: Feeling awkward in company
senses.definition: uneasy in a situation or in someone’s presence
senses.definitionCN: 在某种场合或某人面前感到不自然
senses.example: She felt uncomfortable in such an expensive restaurant.
senses.exampleCN: 在这么贵的餐厅里她感到很不自在。
senses.why: When the body cannot settle, the mind in company cannot settle either.
senses.whyCN: 身体安顿不下来时，在人前的心也安顿不下来。

senses.title: Making others uneasy
senses.definition: used of a silence, a remark, or a truth that embarrasses
senses.definitionCN: 形容让人发窘的沉默、话语或真相
senses.example: There was an uncomfortable pause after his question.
senses.exampleCN: 他那个问题之后有一阵尴尬的停顿。
senses.why: The word turns outward, naming whatever puts the room on edge.
senses.whyCN: 这个词转朝外，指任何让整个房间绷紧的东西。

senses.title: Slightly painful or troubling
senses.definition: of a fact or a feeling, hard to sit with
senses.definitionCN: 就事实或感受而言，难以安然面对
senses.example: The report holds some uncomfortable truths.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告里有一些让人不好受的真相。
senses.why: A fact is like a hard seat: nothing about it can be padded, so it stays uncomfortable.
senses.whyCN: 事实像一张硬座，没有任何地方能垫软，所以它始终让人不好受。

senses.title: Unpleasant to do or wear
senses.definition: awkward to wear or to carry out
senses.definitionCN: 穿戴或施行起来别扭
senses.example: He gave an uncomfortable little bow.
senses.exampleCN: 他很别扭地微微鞠了一躬。
senses.why: An action done with a stiff body looks exactly like an uncomfortable garment.
senses.whyCN: 一个用僵硬身体做出的动作，看起来就像一件不合身的衣服。

intro.en: The word is an English negative of comfort, a Latin-derived verb of strengthening.
intro.cn: 这个词是 comfort 的英语否定形式，而 comfort 源自拉丁语「使强健」的动词。

items.en: Confortare joins con-, together, and fortis, strong, meaning to strengthen.
items.cn: confortare 由 con-（一起）与 fortis（强壮）组成，意为使强健。

items.en: Old French conforter gives the sense of cheering and consoling.
items.cn: 古法语 conforter 带出「鼓舞、安慰」之义。

items.en: English comfort keeps both the body sense and the mental relief.
items.cn: 英语 comfort 同时保留身体与心情两方面的宽解。

items.en: Comfortable and uncomfortable settle into their modern bodily senses in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: comfortable 与 uncomfortable 在十八世纪定型为现代的身体义。

items.en: The social sense of awkwardness grows in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 社交上的「尴尬」义在十九、二十世纪生长出来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the comfort stem, and the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of unease.
note.cn: 形近组共用 comfort 词干，近义组汇集表示不安的形容词。

entries.definition: at ease in body or mind

normalIntro.en: Comfort is the feeling of being strengthened and eased, and the prefix takes that away.
normalIntro.cn: comfort 是被撑住、被放松的感觉，前缀把它抽走。

normal.en: Fortis in Latin means strong, so comfort is a backbone underneath you.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 fortis 意为强壮，comfort 就是脊背下面的一根支撑。

normal.en: Discomfort and uncomfortableness are two nouns for the same missing ease.
normal.cn: discomfort 与 uncomfortableness 是两个名词，说的是同一份缺失的舒服。

normal.en: The adverb uncomfortably often follows feel, sit, or shift.
normal.cn: 副词 uncomfortably 常跟在 feel、sit、shift 之后。

normal.en: An uncomfortable silence is the phrase that carries the social sense.
normal.cn: uncomfortable silence 是承载社交义的那个搭配。

normal.en: English speakers use more uncomfortable rather than a suffixed comparative.
normal.cn: 英语说 more uncomfortable，不用加词尾的比较级。

abstract.en: Sit on a bench too hard for your back and shift every minute.
abstract.cn: 坐在一条硌背的长凳上，每分钟都在挪。

abstract.en: Notice the same shifting in a room after a bad question.
abstract.cn: 注意一个糟糕的问题之后，整个房间同样在挪。

abstract.en: Then feel a truth you cannot make comfortable by argument.
abstract.cn: 再感到一个用争辩也安顿不下来的真相。

examples.en: The seats on the bus were cramped and uncomfortable.
examples.cn: 公交车上的座位又挤又不舒服。

examples.en: He felt uncomfortable when the teacher praised him in front of everyone.
examples.cn: 老师在众人面前表扬他时，他觉得很不好意思。

examples.en: An uncomfortable silence fell over the dinner table.
examples.cn: 饭桌上一时陷入尴尬的沉默。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安扛福特波」——躺着才安，硬要扛着一块福特牌铁板，浑身都不舒服。

root: un-（否定前缀）+ comfortable（源自拉丁语 confortare「使强健」，由 com- + fortis「强壮」构成）；同族有 comfort、discomfort

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from a body that cannot settle, to a mind that cannot settle, to a moment that makes everyone else settle worse.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从安顿不下来的身体，到安顿不下来的心，再到让所有人都更坐不稳的时刻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: shifting on a bench that is too hard.
core.cn: 核心意象：在太硬的板凳上不停挪动。

branches.en: The body branch: hard seats, tight shoes, stiff bows.
branches.cn: 身体分支：硬座、挤脚的鞋、僵硬的鞠躬。

branches.en: The personal branch: unease in a place or in company.
branches.cn: 个人分支：在某个场合或人前的不自在。

branches.en: The social branch: silences and remarks that embarrass a room.
branches.cn: 社交分支：让一屋子人发窘的沉默与话语。

branches.en: The truth branch: facts that cannot be made pleasant.
branches.cn: 真相分支：无法被说得舒服的事实。

branches.en: The plain physical sense of chairs and shoes.
branches.cn: 椅子与鞋子最普通的身体义。

intro.en: A negation prefix on top of a Latin verb of strengthening.
intro.cn: 否定前缀盖在拉丁语的「使强健」动词上。

latinIntro.en: Fortis, strong, also lies behind fort, effort, and reinforce.
latinIntro.cn: fortis（强壮）还支撑着 fort、effort、reinforce 等词。

items.exampleCN: fortis 支撑着 effort 与 fort。
uncomfortable 在正式文章里可加 -ness。

items.example: He felt a stab of discomfort.

definition_zh: 失去知觉的；昏迷的；无意识的；不知不觉的；未察觉的
definition_en: not awake and not aware, or doing something without noticing it
core_image: 灯还亮着，屋里的人却睡着了，谁进门都不知道
scene: 车祸现场，一名骑手倒在路边，脸色发白，叫他也没有回应。The injured cyclist was unconscious when the ambulance arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 unconscious 是「失去知觉的」（第 1 个义项：昏迷不醒、无反应）；句意为救护车到时那位受伤的骑车人已经昏迷。灯亮着而人不省人事，正是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 形容词：失去知觉的；昏迷的
形容词：无意识的；不知不觉的

derivatives.zh: 去掉否定前缀的原词，义为「有意识的；清醒的」
形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「无意识地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「无意识状态」

senses.title: Not awake or responsive
senses.definition: in a state like deep sleep, with no response to people or pain
senses.definitionCN: 处于类似深睡的状态，对人与疼痛都没有反应
senses.example: He was unconscious for two days after the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 跌倒后他昏迷了两天。
senses.why: Conscious comes from Latin conscire, to know together with oneself, so un- removes all inner awareness.
senses.whyCN: conscious 源自拉丁语 conscire（与自己一同知道），un- 抽走了全部内在觉知。

senses.title: Done without noticing
senses.definition: done without intending or noticing it
senses.definitionCN: 做的时候既无意，也没有察觉
senses.example: She has an unconscious habit of touching her hair.
senses.exampleCN: 她有个无意识摸头发的习惯。
senses.why: When the knowing part of the mind sleeps, the body still acts, and that action is called unconscious.
senses.whyCN: 知道的那部分睡着了，身体仍在动，这种动作就叫无意识。

senses.title: Not aware of something present
senses.definition: not realizing that something is there
senses.definitionCN: 没有意识到某物的存在
senses.example: They were unconscious of the risk they ran.
senses.exampleCN: 他们没有察觉自己冒的风险。
senses.why: Awareness can be switched off by inattention as well as by injury.
senses.whyCN: 觉知既可能被伤损关掉，也可能被疏忽关掉。

senses.title: The hidden part of the mind
senses.definition: in psychology, the store of feelings and memories outside awareness
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中指意识之外的感受与记忆的储藏处
senses.example: Fear of failure can live in the unconscious for years.
senses.exampleCN: 对失败的恐惧可以在潜意识里住很多年。
senses.why: Since unconscious names what awareness does not reach, it becomes a noun for the region beyond it.
senses.whyCN: 既然 unconscious 指觉知够不到的地方，它就转作名词，指那片区域本身。

senses.title: Showing feelings one does not admit
senses.definition: revealing a feeling that the person is not admitting
senses.definitionCN: 显出当事人自己并不承认的情绪
senses.example: There was an unconscious coldness in his reply.
senses.exampleCN: 他的回答里透着一种不自觉的冷淡。
senses.why: The face reports what the mind has not yet admitted, so the expression is unconscious in the strict sense.
senses.whyCN: 脸会把心里还没承认的事报出来，因此这种表情是严格意义上的「无意识」。

intro.en: The word is an English negative of a Latin verb of shared knowing.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「共同知道」动词的英语否定形式。

items.en: Scire means to know, and conscire means to know with oneself, to be aware.
items.cn: scire 意为知道，conscire 意为与自己一同知道，即有所觉察。

items.en: Conscius is one who knows, either as a witness or as an accomplice.
items.cn: conscius 指知情者，可以是证人，也可以是同谋。

items.en: Conscious enters English in the seventeenth century with the sense of being aware.
items.cn: conscious 在十七世纪进入英语，意为有所觉察。

items.en: Unconscious follows as its negative, used first for the absence of response.
items.cn: unconscious 作为否定随后出现，最初指失去反应。

items.en: Psychology from the nineteenth century makes the noun unconscious a technical term.
items.cn: 十九世纪起心理学把名词 unconscious 变成术语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sci- root of knowing, and the near-meaning group gathers states of unawareness.
note.cn: 形近组共用表示「知道」的 sci- 词根，近义组汇集无察觉的状态。

entries.definition: the inner sense of right and wrong

normalIntro.en: Scire is Latin for know, so an unconscious person has no knowing at all, or none in that moment.
normalIntro.cn: scire 是拉丁语的「知道」，unconscious 的人便一点也不知道，或那一刻不知道。

normal.en: Conscious and conscience both come from knowing, one of the world and one of right and wrong.
normal.cn: conscious 与 conscience 都出自「知道」，一个知世界，一个知善恶。

normal.en: To be knocked unconscious is to have awareness switched off by force.
normal.cn: knocked unconscious 指觉知被外力关掉。

normal.en: An unconscious habit runs while the mind is busy elsewhere.
normal.cn: unconscious habit 在心神忙于别处时照常运行。

normal.en: In psychology the unconscious is a noun, the store below awareness.
normal.cn: 心理学里 the unconscious 是名词，指意识之下的储藏。

normal.en: Unconsciously is the adverb for acts done without noticing.
normal.cn: unconsciously 是副词，指没察觉地做出。

abstract.en: See a room with the light on and the person asleep in a chair.
abstract.cn: 看见一间灯还亮着的屋子，人却在椅子上睡着。

abstract.en: Watch a hand reach for the hair without the owner looking.
abstract.cn: 看一只手在主人没留神时去摸头发。

abstract.en: Then picture a cellar under that room, full of things never brought up.
abstract.cn: 再想象屋子底下有个地窖，装满从未搬上来的东西。

examples.en: The boxer was unconscious before the count reached five.
examples.cn: 数到五之前那名拳手已经失去知觉。

examples.en: He was unconscious of how loud his voice had become.
examples.cn: 他没意识到自己的嗓门已经这么大了。

examples.en: She tidied the desk unconsciously while talking on the phone.
examples.cn: 打电话时她无意识地把桌子收拾了一遍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺坑舍斯」——俺掉进坑里，舍了什么也没感觉，人事不省。

root: un-（否定前缀）+ conscious（拉丁语 conscire「与自己一同知道」，由 com- + scire「知道」构成）；同族有 consciousness、conscience

sensesIntro.en: Every sense removes or lowers awareness, from a body that cannot respond to a mind that does not notice.
sensesIntro.cn: 每个义项都在撤走或降低觉知：从毫无反应的身体，到毫无察觉的心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit room with no one awake in it.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯亮着却没有清醒的人在屋内。

branches.en: The body branch: knocked out and unresponsive.
branches.cn: 身体分支：被打昏、毫无反应。

branches.en: The habit branch: actions and expressions the person does not notice.
branches.cn: 习惯分支：当事人没察觉的动作与表情。

branches.en: The perception branch: a risk or fact never registered.
branches.cn: 感知分支：从未登记进来的风险或事实。

branches.en: The psychology branch, where the word becomes a noun.
branches.cn: 心理学分支：这个词在此作名词。

branches.en: The medical sense of a patient who cannot be roused.
branches.cn: 医学义：唤不醒的病人。

intro.en: A negation prefix on a Latin word for knowing with oneself.
intro.cn: 否定前缀盖在拉丁语「与自己一同知道」的词上。

latinIntro.en: The sci- root of knowing also gives science, conscience, and conscious.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「知道」的 sci- 词根还生出 science、conscience、conscious。

items.exampleCN: scire 支撑着 science 与 conscience。

items.example: She was conscious of the noise.

definition_zh: 不受控制的；不加克制的；未受管制的；无节制的
definition_en: not kept within limits by anyone or anything
core_image: 缰绳脱了手，马车顺着坡自己往下冲
scene: 山路上，送货的三轮车刹车失灵，车主只能大声让路人躲开。Uncontrolled spending left the family without savings.
sceneCN: 这里 uncontrolled 是「不受控制的」（第 1 个义项：失去约束）；句意为无节制的开销让这家人没有存款。脱手的缰绳让车自己冲下坡，正是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 形容词：不受控制的；失控的
形容词：未受管制的；未经检查的

derivatives.zh: 去掉否定前缀的原词，义为「控制；管理」
过去分词作形容词，义为「受控制的」
动词加 -er 构成，义为「控制者；控制器」

senses.title: Not kept in check
senses.definition: of a feeling or force, running on without restraint
senses.definitionCN: 就情绪或力量而言，不受约束地继续下去
senses.example: His uncontrolled temper frightened the class.
senses.exampleCN: 他那股不加克制的脾气让全班害怕。
senses.why: Control comes from a medieval roll kept for checking accounts, so un- means the roll is no longer being checked.
senses.whyCN: control 源自中世纪用于核对账目的卷册，un- 意味着这本卷册不再被核对。

senses.title: Not regulated by authority
senses.definition: not supervised or limited by an official body
senses.definitionCN: 没有官方机构的监督或限制
senses.example: Uncontrolled dumping polluted the river.
senses.exampleCN: 不受管制的倾倒污染了这条河。
senses.why: Where no ledger is kept, nothing is checked, and a rule that is not checked is no rule.
senses.whyCN: 没有账簿的地方就无人核对，而不被核对的规则等于没有规则。

senses.title: Growing or spreading without limit
senses.definition: increasing with no limit or plan
senses.definitionCN: 没有限度或计划地增加
senses.example: The city faces uncontrolled building on its edges.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市面临边缘地带无节制的建设。
senses.why: Growth that no one measures simply keeps adding itself, brick after brick.
senses.whyCN: 无人度量的增长只会一块砖接一块砖地自己加上去。

senses.title: Not restrained in the body
senses.definition: of movement, shaking, or crying that the body cannot stop
senses.definitionCN: 指抖动、哭泣等身体动作止不下来
senses.example: Uncontrolled shivering followed the fever.
senses.exampleCN: 发烧之后接着是不停的发抖。
senses.why: When the reins are gone, the body no longer obeys the will.
senses.whyCN: 缰绳一断，身体就不再听意志的指挥。

senses.title: Lacking a comparison group in research
senses.definition: of a trial, carried out without a comparison group to check results
senses.definitionCN: 指试验没有设对照组来核对结果
senses.example: An uncontrolled trial cannot prove the drug works.
senses.exampleCN: 未设对照组的试验无法证明这种药有效。
senses.why: In science control means the standard kept for comparison, so uncontrolled means no such standard exists.
senses.whyCN: 科学里 control 指用于比较的标准样本，uncontrolled 就是没有这个标准。

intro.en: The word is the past participle of control with a negative prefix.
intro.cn: 这个词是 control 的过去分词加否定前缀。

items.en: Contrarotulus is a roll kept against a duplicate roll for checking accounts.
items.cn: contrarotulus 是与另一本副本卷册并置、用于核对账目的卷册。

items.en: Old French contrerolle carries the account-checking sense of the word.
items.cn: 古法语 contrerolle 保留了核对账目之义。

items.en: English control first means to check accounts, then to direct anything.
items.cn: 英语 control 先指核对账目，后指对任何事物的支配。

items.en: Uncontrolled appears in the eighteenth century for what escapes checking.
items.cn: uncontrolled 在十八世纪出现，指逃出核对的东西。

items.en: Science adopts controlled and uncontrolled for trials in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 二十世纪，科学界用 controlled 与 uncontrolled 称呼试验。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the control family, and the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of unrestrained force.
note.cn: 形近组展示 control 词族，近义组汇集表示约束失效的形容词。

entries.definition: a person or device that controls

normalIntro.en: Control began as a copy ledger kept for checking, and losing it means losing the check.
normalIntro.cn: control 最初是一本用来核对的副本账簿，丢了它就丢了核对。

normal.en: Contra- means against and rotulus is a roll, so control is a check roll held beside the account.
normal.cn: contra- 意为相对，rotulus 是卷册，control 就是放在账册旁的核对卷。

normal.en: The controlled object of a verb and the controlled style of writing both come from that check.
normal.cn: 动词的宾语叫 object，写作的自制叫 controlled，都出自这层核对。

normal.en: Uncontrolled laughter and uncontrolled growth share the lack of a check.
normal.cn: uncontrolled laughter 与 uncontrolled growth 共享「缺少核对」这一层。

normal.en: Controlled experiment and uncontrolled trial are the two poles in research.
normal.cn: controlled experiment 与 uncontrolled trial 是研究里的两极。

normal.en: English says more uncontrolled, not uncontrolleder.
normal.cn: 英语说 more uncontrolled，不说 uncontrolleder。

abstract.en: Feel reins slip out of your fingers on a slope.
abstract.cn: 感觉缰绳在坡上从指间滑脱。

abstract.en: Watch a garden grow over its fence in one summer.
abstract.cn: 看一座花园在一个夏天里长过围栏。

abstract.en: Then see a ledger left open with no one checking it.
abstract.cn: 再看一本摊开无人核对的账册。

examples.en: Uncontrolled fires have destroyed large areas of forest.
examples.cn: 失控的大火毁掉了大片森林。

examples.en: Her uncontrolled laughter filled the whole corridor.
examples.cn: 她止不住的笑声传遍了整条走廊。

examples.en: The drug was tested in an uncontrolled trial only.
examples.cn: 这种药只在未设对照组的试验中测试过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安控球得」——球一旦安不住，控不住就得看着它滚下坡。

root: un-（否定前缀）+ controlled（control 加 -ed；control 源自中世纪拉丁语 contrarotulus「核对卷册」，由 contra-「相对」+ rotulus「卷」构成）

sensesIntro.en: Whatever escapes a check is uncontrolled: a temper, a market, a fire, a shaking body, or a trial without a comparison group.
sensesIntro.cn: 任何逃出核对的东西都是 uncontrolled：脾气、市场、火、发抖的身体，或没有对照组的试验。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: reins slipping free on a downhill road.
core.cn: 核心意象：下坡路上脱了手的缰绳。

branches.en: The feeling branch: anger and laughter that will not stop.
branches.cn: 情绪分支：止不住的怒气与笑声。

branches.en: The authority branch: dumping and building no one supervises.
branches.cn: 权力分支：无人监管的倾倒与建设。

branches.en: The growth branch: expansion with no plan.
branches.cn: 增长分支：没有计划的扩张。

branches.en: The body branch: shivering the will cannot stop.
branches.cn: 身体分支：意志止不住的颤抖。

branches.en: The research branch, where control means a comparison group.
branches.cn: 研究分支：这里的 control 指对照组。

intro.en: A negation prefix on a participle of checking and directing.
intro.cn: 否定前缀盖在表示核对与支配的分词上。

latinIntro.en: The roll image in contrarotulus survives in the modern word.
latinIntro.cn: contrarotulus 里那卷账簿的意象一直留在现代词中。

items.example: Contra- sits at the front of control.
items.exampleCN: contra- 位于 control 词首。

items.example: The roll was the account book.

definition_zh: 揭开；掀开；发现；揭露；查明
definition_en: to remove a cover, or to find out something that was hidden
core_image: 把盖布一把掀开，底下原本藏着的东西露在光里
scene: 考古队在沙地里刮了一上午，终于露出半块刻着字的石板边缘。The reporter uncovered a series of secret payments.
sceneCN: 这里 uncover 是「发现、揭露」（第 2 个义项：把藏起来的事查出来）；句意为记者揭露了一连串秘密付款。掀开盖布让底下露出来，正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 动词分词作形容词，义为「无遮盖的；被揭发的」
动词加 -ing 构成名词，义为「揭露；发掘」
同源近义词，义为「发现」

senses.title: To take a cover off something
senses.definition: to lift or remove the thing lying over an object
senses.definitionCN: 把盖在某物上面的东西提起或拿走
senses.example: He uncovered the pot to let the steam out.
senses.exampleCN: 他把锅盖揭开让蒸汽散出去。
senses.why: The verb is un- plus cover, so it simply undoes the covering.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是 un- 加 cover，就是把「盖」这个动作反过来。

senses.title: To find out something hidden
senses.definition: to discover a fact or plan that someone wanted concealed
senses.definitionCN: 发现某人本想隐瞒的事实或计划
senses.example: The audit uncovered serious errors.
senses.exampleCN: 审计查出了严重错误。
senses.why: Once the cover is physically lifted, the figurative cover of secrecy behaves the same way.
senses.whyCN: 盖布既然能被掀开，机密这层盖布也一样。

senses.title: To make a truth public
senses.definition: to bring a hidden wrongdoing into public view
senses.definitionCN: 使隐秘的恶行进入公众视野
senses.example: Two journalists uncovered the whole scheme.
senses.exampleCN: 两名记者揭发了整个计划。
senses.why: Muckrakers and auditors alike use the word once the covering image is in place.
senses.whyCN: 只要「盖布」这个比喻立住了，扒粪记者与审计员都会用这个词。

senses.title: To show a hidden part naturally
senses.definition: of natural forces, to leave something visible by moving what lies over it
senses.definitionCN: 指自然力量把覆盖之物移开，使某物可见
senses.example: The rain uncovered the old stone path.
senses.exampleCN: 这场雨把那条古老的石板路冲了出来。
senses.why: Water and wind do the uncovering without any intention at all.
senses.whyCN: 风雨本无意图，却完成了揭开这件事。

senses.title: To leave oneself unprotected
senses.definition: to put a body or a position in the open with no shield
senses.definitionCN: 把身体或阵地放在毫无遮挡之处
senses.example: The soldiers edged forward, uncovered by any wall.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们向前挪动，没有任何墙作掩护。
senses.why: To have no cover is to be uncovered, so the military sense is the literal picture standing alone.
senses.whyCN: 没有掩护就是无遮盖，因此这个军事义只是把字面画面单独摆出来。

intro.en: The word is built in English from un- and cover, whose ultimate source is Latin.
intro.cn: 这个词在英语里由 un- 与 cover 组合而成，而 cover 的源头是拉丁语。

items.en: Cooperire joins com-, fully, and operire, to close or hide, meaning to cover completely.
items.cn: cooperire 由 com-（完全）与 operire（关闭、遮盖）组成，意为完全盖住。

items.en: Old French covrir and a shorter form give English cover.
items.cn: 古法语 covrir 及其较短形式给英语带来 cover。

items.en: Cover appears in English in the twelfth century with the sense of covering a thing.
items.cn: cover 在十二世纪进入英语，意为盖住某物。

items.en: Uncover is formed by plain prefixing, first for physical lifting.
items.cn: uncover 由简单加前缀构成，最初用于实物掀盖。

items.en: From the nineteenth century it is common for exposing scandals.
items.cn: 十九世纪起，用它来指揭发丑闻变得常见。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cover stem, and the near-meaning group gathers verbs of disclosure.
note.cn: 形近组共用 cover 词干，近义组汇集表示揭露的动词。

entries.definition: to find for the first time
the extent to which something is covered

normalIntro.en: The word is simply the undo of covering, first of pots and then of secrets.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词不过是「盖」的反动作，先掀锅盖，再掀秘密。

normal.en: Un- plus cover reads as take the cover off, exactly as its letters suggest.
normal.cn: un- 加 cover 读作把盖拿走，正如字面所写。

normal.en: Discover and uncover both build on the same Latin root of hiding.
normal.cn: discover 与 uncover 同建在一个表示「遮盖」的拉丁词根上。

normal.en: Uncovered is also an adjective for a field with nothing over it.
normal.cn: uncovered 也可作形容词，指没有遮盖的空地。

normal.en: Journalists uncover schemes; engineers uncover faults in a design.
normal.cn: 记者揭露阴谋，工程师查设计里的缺陷。

normal.en: The past tense is uncovered, a regular -ed form.
normal.cn: 过去式是 uncovered，规则的加 -ed 形式。

abstract.en: Take a corner of the cloth and lift it in one motion.
abstract.cn: 捏住盖布一角，一下掀起来。

abstract.en: See beneath it something already there, only unknown.
abstract.cn: 看见底下早就在，只是没人知道。

abstract.en: Then watch rain wash soil off an old stone path.
abstract.cn: 再看雨水冲掉石板路上的泥土。

examples.en: The police uncovered a network of false documents.
examples.cn: 警方查出了一个假证件网络。

examples.en: Wind had uncovered the roots of the fallen tree.
examples.cn: 风把倒下的树的根露了出来。

examples.en: She uncovered the tray to show us the cake.
examples.cn: 她把托盘盖掀开，让我们看那块蛋糕。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安卡佛」——安好盖子再卡上，一掀开，佛就现身了。

root: un-（反向前缀）+ cover（古法语 covrir，源自拉丁语 cooperire，由 com-「完全」+ operire「遮盖」构成）

sensesIntro.en: All senses undo a covering, whether a lid, a secrecy, a layer of soil, or a shield.
sensesIntro.cn: 所有义项都在解除一层遮盖：锅盖、保密、土层，或掩护。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cloth pulled back from what lay beneath.
core.cn: 核心意象：盖布被掀开，露出底下的东西。

branches.en: The physical branch: pots, trays, and lids.
branches.cn: 实物分支：锅、托盘与盖子。

branches.en: The inquiry branch: audits and police work that find facts.
branches.cn: 调查分支：审计与侦查查出事实。

branches.en: The public branch: reporters exposing a scheme.
branches.cn: 公开分支：记者揭发阴谋。

branches.en: The nature branch: rain and wind uncovering stone.
branches.cn: 自然分支：风雨冲露出石板。

branches.en: The military branch, where no wall gives cover.
branches.cn: 军事分支：没有墙可作掩护。

intro.en: A reversing prefix on a verb of hiding, itself from Latin.
intro.cn: 反向前缀盖在一个表示遮盖的动词上，该动词源自拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: Operire, to close, also lies behind cover, covert, and discover.
latinIntro.cn: operire（关闭）还支撑着 cover、covert、discover。

items.exampleCN: uncover 是 cover 的反动作。

items.example: The boat stood uncovered all winter.
items.exampleCN: 那条船整个冬天都露天放着。

items.example: The uncovering of the tomb took years.
items.exampleCN: 这座墓的发掘花了好几年。

definition_zh: 经历；经受；承受；（医）接受（治疗、手术）
definition_en: to go through something difficult or a process that changes you
core_image: 一个人低头走进一条昏暗的通道，出来时已经不同了
scene: 手术室外的长椅上，家属们安静地等着，护士说病人正在里面接受一次大手术。She had to undergo two operations in one year.
sceneCN: 这里 undergo 是「接受（手术）」（第 3 个义项：承受某种过程）；句意为她一年里不得不接受两次手术。低头走进昏暗通道，出来时已不同，正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 过去分词，义为「已经历」
过去式，义为「经历了」
现在分词，义为「正在经历」

senses.title: To go through an experience
senses.definition: to pass through a period or an event that acts on you
senses.definitionCN: 穿过一段时期或一件事，并受其作用
senses.example: The town underwent great changes in the war.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城在战争中经历了巨大变化。
senses.why: Under means beneath and go means move, so to undergo is to pass beneath a weight and come out the other side.
senses.whyCN: under 意为在其下，go 意为行进，合起来就是从那重压底下穿过、再从另一头出来。

senses.title: To be subjected to a process
senses.definition: to be put through a process such as testing or repair
senses.definitionCN: 被放入检查、修理之类的流程中
senses.example: Every engine undergoes a final check.
senses.exampleCN: 每台发动机都要经过最后检查。
senses.why: A process laid over you is a weight over you, and the two images meet.
senses.whyCN: 加在你身上的一套流程就是压在你身上的一重压，两个意象在此汇合。

senses.title: To receive medical treatment
senses.definition: to have a treatment performed on one’s body
senses.definitionCN: 让人在自己身体上施行某项治疗
senses.example: He underwent a heart operation last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 去年春天他接受了一次心脏手术。
senses.why: In medicine the word keeps the sense of letting something heavy pass over the body.
senses.whyCN: 在医学里，这个词保留了「让沉重之物从身体上经过」的意思。

senses.title: To endure hardship or suffering
senses.definition: to bear pain or loss over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间里承受疼痛或损失
senses.example: The villagers underwent years of shortage.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们过了好几年短缺的日子。
senses.why: Hardship is a weight that stays on for a long time, and the word names the bearing of it.
senses.whyCN: 艰难是长时间压着的一副重量，这个词指的正是把它担过去。

senses.title: To suffer a change of state
senses.definition: of a thing, to pass into a different state through a process
senses.definitionCN: 指某物经由过程转入另一种状态
senses.example: The metal undergoes expansion when heated.
senses.exampleCN: 金属受热时会发生膨胀。
senses.why: Whatever the process is, the subject comes out different, which is why the word suits changes.
senses.whyCN: 不论过程为何，主体走过之后都会变样，所以它特别适合说变化。

intro.en: The word is an English compound of under and go, first recorded in Old English.
intro.cn: 这个词是 under 与 go 的英语复合词，最早见于古英语。

items.en: Undergan means to undergo or to undertake, built from under and gan, to go.
items.cn: undergān 意为承受或着手，由 under 与 gān（走）构成。

items.en: The prefix under carried the idea of coming under something.
items.cn: 前缀 under 带着「进到某物之下」的意思。

items.en: Middle English undergon keeps the sense of passing through hardship.
items.cn: 中古英语 undergon 保留「穿过艰难」之义。

items.en: The past forms underwent and undergone settle into their modern spelling.
items.cn: 过去式与过去分词定型为 underwent 与 undergone。

items.en: Medical usage for treatment grows in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 表示「接受治疗」的医学用法在十九、二十世纪兴盛。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers under- compounds, and the near-meaning group collects verbs of experiencing.
note.cn: 形近组汇集 under- 复合词，近义组汇集表示经历的动词。

entries.definition: to take on a duty or task
to lie beneath as a cause

normalIntro.en: Under plus go: you go beneath a thing and come out on the far side.
normalIntro.cn: under 加 go：从一件东西底下走过去，再从另一头出来。

normal.en: Undergo is irregular: underwent today, undergone in the past participle.
normal.cn: undergo 不规则：过去式 underwent，过去分词 undergone。

normal.en: The word almost always takes an article with a process, as in undergo an operation.
normal.cn: 这个词接过程名词时通常带冠词，如 undergo an operation。

normal.en: Undertake takes on a duty, while undergo receives an experience.
normal.cn: undertake 是主动承担，undergo 是被动承受。

normal.en: Hospitals use it constantly: patients undergo tests, scans, and surgery.
normal.cn: 医院里用得极多：病人 undergo 检查、扫描、手术。

normal.en: Undergo change is the standard formal way to say something was altered.
normal.cn: undergo change 是表示「发生了变化」的正式说法。

abstract.en: Step down into a dim passage and keep walking.
abstract.cn: 低头走进一条昏暗的通道，一直往前走。

abstract.en: Feel the walls close while your own shape changes.
abstract.cn: 感觉两侧墙收拢，而你自己的形状在变。

abstract.en: Come out at the other end wearing that change.
abstract.cn: 从另一头出来时，已经带着那层变化。

examples.en: The bridge will undergo repairs this summer.
examples.cn: 这座桥今年夏天将进行维修。

examples.en: Patients must undergo a full examination first.
examples.cn: 病人必须先接受全面检查。

examples.en: The old factory underwent a complete change of use.
examples.cn: 那座旧厂房经历了彻底的用途改变。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安得够」——能不能安得够稳，只看你经不经得住这一程。

root: 古英语 under（在下）+ gān（走），undergān 意为承受、着手；过去式 underwent，过去分词 undergone

sensesIntro.en: In every sense the subject passes beneath something, an event, a process, an operation, or hardship.
sensesIntro.cn: 在每一个义项里，主体都从某样东西底下经过：一件事、一套流程、一次手术，或一段艰难。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: walking through a dim passage and changing inside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：穿过昏暗通道，在里面被改变。

branches.en: The change branch: events and heat that alter the subject.
branches.cn: 变化分支：改变主体的事件与热。

branches.en: The process branch: checks and repairs laid over a thing.
branches.cn: 流程分支：加在物上的检查与修理。

branches.en: The medical branch: operations and scans on the body.
branches.cn: 医学分支：在身体上做的手术与扫描。

branches.en: The hardship branch: years of shortage borne quietly.
branches.cn: 艰难分支：默默承受的多年短缺。

branches.en: The common sense of living through a period.
branches.cn: 常用义：度过一段时期。

intro.en: Two Old English pieces joined: a preposition of position and a verb of moving.
intro.cn: 两块古英语部件拼合：一个方位介词与一个走动的动词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source, so the Latin list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 此词没有拉丁语来源，故拉丁同源词一栏留空。

items.exampleCN: 信任是这笔交易的基础。

definition_zh: 本科生；大学生；（作定语）本科的
definition_en: a student at a university who has not yet taken a first degree
core_image: 阶梯上还没拿到第一块牌子的那个年轻人
scene: 九月开学，图书馆门前排着长队，手里拿着新学生证的都是刚入学的年轻人。She was still an undergraduate when she wrote her first book.
sceneCN: 这里 undergraduate 是「本科生」（第 1 个义项：尚未取得学位的大学生）；句意为她写第一本书时还是本科生。还没拿到第一块牌子的年轻人，正是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 形容词：本科的；大学生的

derivatives.zh: 去掉前缀的原词，义为「毕业生；研究生」
口语缩略形式，义为「本科生」
